filo synced
filo synced add DIR [-y]
filo synced remove DIR [-y]
filo synced ignore DIR

  A synced directory is one a sync service (any of them) shares between devices.
  Marking it lets the devices that run Filo share their decisions about its
  files: each keeps its own register, and writes the decisions it makes there to
  its own signed journal in DIR/.filo/, which the sync service copies and the
  other devices read. A journal only records decisions: it never deletes,
  renames or moves a file.

  add marks DIR, a directory in a root, when it has no mark. When it has one
  (the sync service brought it from another device), add shows the devices whose
  journals are there, with their key fingerprints to compare with filo device on
  each, and asks before trusting them and joining. When it holds the mark of a
  synced directory this device joined elsewhere, which is gone from there, add
  asks whether it moved. One synced directory cannot hold another.

  Every scan notes the marks it finds; a mark this device has not joined is
  reported until it is joined, or ignored with ignore. remove stops this device
  sharing decisions in DIR (its files and the journals stay), or forgets that a
  mark was ignored. filo synced lists the synced directories, what is wrong in
  each, and the marks found.

Flags
  -y                       add and remove: without asking
